刑 concerns criminal punishment or a legal sentence. Here "sentence" means a penalty imposed for an offense, not a grammatical sentence. In 刑事 けいじ, it contributes the criminal-law association: the whole word can name a police detective or concern criminal matters.

Modern-shape mnemonic, not etymology: Picture the squared-off left part as a rule board beside the blade radical 刂, a reminder of a legal penalty. This invented association does not establish the character's history or a phonetic component.
ケイ
刑事 けいじ — police detective; criminal matters; 刑罰 けいばつ — criminal punishment; penalty

The frozen KANJIDIC2 metadata lists ケイ and no kun readings. Other dictionaries have broader reading coverage: Digital Daijisen also records ギョウ, as in the historical ministry name 刑部省 ぎょうぶしょう. That does not change the reading of 刑事 to ぎょうじ.
刑事 けいじ — police detective; criminal matters
刑 けい — penalty; sentence
刑罰 けいばつ — criminal punishment; penalty
刑法 けいほう — criminal law; penal code
刀 is the dictionary radical; its visible right-side form here is 刂. Compare 形, with three slanting strokes 彡 on the right, and 型, with 土 underneath the 刑-shaped upper part.
The main lesson here is punishment. Dictionaries also record older model/form-related senses of 刑; the shape comparisons above are not a claim that 刑, 型 and 形 have never overlapped in meaning.
刑事 also has the slang whole-word reading でか. Learn it as a separate reading of the whole word, not as a kun reading of 刑 alone. The linked article's primary reading remains けいじ.
In legal expressions, 刑事 does not mean "criminal" as a noun naming an offender. Use the surrounding noun and sentence role to distinguish criminal matters from the detective.

Metadata: KANJIDIC2, 2026-11-02 snapshot. Word families: JMdict, entries 1249610, 1249660, 1249780, 1249790, 1008360 and 2256510. Character readings and wider senses: Digital Daijisen, 刑; compound senses: 刑事.
刑事 けいじ — police detective; criminal matters
刑事 has two related uses: a noun for a police detective, and "criminal" in legal expressions concerning criminal matters.
刑事が目撃者に話を聞いています。 (けいじがもくげきしゃにはなしをきいています。) - A detective is talking to a witness.
これは刑事事件です。 (これはけいじじけんです。) - This is a criminal case.
In the first example, 刑事 is a person. In 刑事事件, it qualifies 事件 (じけん), "case/incident"; it does not mean "a detective's incident." Another useful combination is 刑事裁判 (けいじさいばん), "criminal trial."
刑 contributes criminal punishment, and 事 contributes a matter or affair. The legal meaning is therefore a helpful guide to the compound. The on readings are ケイ + ジ.

警官 (けいかん) means a police officer, a broader role than detective. 探偵 (たんてい) can refer to a detective such as a private investigator. For legal matters, 民事 (みんじ), "civil," contrasts with 刑事; it is not an opposite kind of police officer.

Use the surrounding noun and sentence role to separate the two senses. 刑事が来た (けいじがきた) means a detective came. 刑事事件 concerns criminal law. Neither use means "criminal" as a noun naming the person who committed an offense.

事 means "matter, affair, thing to be done", and from there "business", "incident" and "fact". The early form is usually explained as a hand holding a tool or a pennant-like object, in the sense of "to serve, to do a task", but scholars disagree on the details, so treat the picture as uncertain. It is filed under 亅 (the hook stroke) only for dictionary purposes; the hook does not carry the meaning.
ジ
食事 しょくじ, 大事 だいじ, 火事 かじ, 事故 じこ, 事件 じけん
ズ
rare, e.g. 好事家 こうずか (a dilettante, an enthusiast)
こと
事 こと (a matter), 大事なこと (an important matter), 仕事 しごと (voiced: ごと)
食事 しょくじ — a meal
仕事 しごと — work, job
火事 かじ — fire (a blaze)
百科事典 ひゃっかじてん — encyclopedia
刑事 けいじ — police detective; criminal matters

事 (こと) is an abstract matter or an act, while 物 (もの) is a concrete thing. 事 also serves as a formal noun (the こと-nominalizer) but is usually written in kana in that role; see the koto and wake article.
仕事 しごと is read with the kun reading (voiced ごと), while 食事 and 火事 use ジ.
Look-alikes: 事 has a vertical stroke with a hook running through the whole character, with 一 and a box-like part above it; compare 力 and 話, which are not related in shape.
